articles.title: Comasa acompanha lançamento da Tukan e nova geração da Amarok em Barretos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo Comasa confere na Festa do Peão de Barretos as novidades da Volkswagen no segmento de picapes, como a inédita Tukan e a nova Amarok.
articles.summary: Grupo Comasa confere na Festa do Peão de Barretos as novidades da Volkswagen no segmento de picapes, como a inédita Tukan e a nova Amarok.
articles.body:
Grupo Comasa acompanha os lançamentos de picapes da Volkswagen na 71ª Festa do Peão de Barretos — Foto: Comasa/Divulgação

O Grupo Comasa esteve presente na 71ª Festa do Peão de Barretos , acompanhando de perto as principais novidades apresentadas pela Volkswagen durante um dos maiores eventos do país. Montadora oficial do Circuito Sertanejo 2026, a marca escolheu Barretos como palco para destacar sua nova estratégia no segmento de picapes, com a apresentação da inédita Tukan , nas versões cabine simples e cabine dupla, além da antecipação de detalhes da nova geração da Amarok , prevista para chegar ao mercado em 2027. A presença no evento permitiu ao Grupo Comasa conhecer de perto os lançamentos que devem reforçar a atuação da Volkswagen no segmento e ampliar seu portfólio nos próximos anos.

Segundo o CEO do Grupo Comasa, Eduardo Freire , a participação no evento foi uma oportunidade de acompanhar diretamente os próximos passos da Volkswagen e compreender a dimensão da ofensiva preparada pela montadora para um segmento estratégico do mercado brasileiro.

“Foi muito importante estar em Barretos e presenciar tudo aquilo que a Volkswagen está preparando. A marca está entrando em uma ofensiva muito forte no segmento de picapes e nós teremos novidades extremamente relevantes a partir do próximo ano. São produtos que atendem desde quem precisa de um veículo para o trabalho até o consumidor que procura uma picape com tecnologia, conforto e uma proposta mais voltada ao lazer e ao estilo de vida”, destaca.

Inédita picape Tukan terá opções de cabine simples para o trabalho e cabine dupla com foco em conforto — Foto: Comasa/Divulgação

Um dos principais destaques foi a apresentação da Volkswagen Tukan , nova picape desenvolvida no Brasil e que chegará ao mercado no primeiro semestre de 2027. O modelo será oferecido em versões de cabine simples e dupla, buscando atender perfis distintos de consumidores . A cabine simples terá uma proposta mais voltada ao uso profissional, enquanto as configurações mais equipadas da cabine dupla terão características de conforto e tecnologia voltadas também ao uso cotidiano.

Segundo Eduardo, essa diversidade de versões amplia a presença da Volkswagen em um mercado que tem ganhado cada vez mais relevância.

“A versão cabine simples tem uma vocação muito forte para o trabalho, com maior robustez, capacidade de carga e soluções pensadas para quem utiliza o veículo como ferramenta no dia a dia. Já a cabine dupla traz uma proposta mais lifestyle, quase como um SUV com caçamba, reunindo conforto, tecnologia e versatilidade. É uma plataforma totalmente nova e que abre uma possibilidade muito grande para a Volkswagen”, explica.

Entre as mudanças técnicas antecipadas para a Tukan estão soluções voltadas ao aumento da capacidade de carga e da resistência do conjunto, incluindo alterações na suspensão traseira . O modelo será construído sobre a plataforma MQB e deverá contar, nas versões mais equipadas, com motorização 1.5 TSI Evo2 associada a um sistema híbrido leve.

Nova Amarok 800 TSI contará com tecnologia híbrida plug-in e potência superior a 470 cavalos — Foto: Comasa/Divulgação

Outro grande destaque em Barretos foi a nova geração da Amarok , apresentada ainda camuflada durante o evento. A Volkswagen confirmou que o modelo chegará em 2027 e será eletrificado. Entre as versões em desenvolvimento está a chamada Amarok 800 TSI , que deverá utilizar sistema híbrido plug-in, com potência superior a 470 cavalos e torque próximo de 800 Nm, reforçando a proposta de elevar ainda mais o desempenho da picape.

“A Amarok sempre foi reconhecida pela força e pelo desempenho. Agora estamos falando de uma nova geração ainda mais potente e com eletrificação. É uma evolução muito grande e que mostra a ambição da Volkswagen para os próximos anos. A expectativa é termos esses produtos muito em breve também em nossas lojas para apresentar aos nossos clientes”, ressalta Eduardo.

A ofensiva faz parte da estratégia da Volkswagen para ampliar sua participação no mercado brasileiro e disputar a liderança do setor. A própria montadora já destacou que a renovação de sua linha de picapes será uma das frentes centrais para seu crescimento na América do Sul, região que passou a participar de forma ainda mais ativa no desenvolvimento, engenharia, testes e validação dos novos modelos.

Ainda segundo Eduardo, acompanhar essas novidades diretamente em Barretos também permite antecipar tendências e preparar suas equipes para a chegada dos próximos lançamentos .

“Estamos muito felizes com o momento da Volkswagen e com os resultados que a marca vem conquistando. Temos uma presença muito forte nas regiões em que atuamos e esses novos produtos chegam para ampliar ainda mais as nossas possibilidades. São lançamentos que podem nos ajudar a manter nossa liderança e conquistar novos clientes”, finaliza.

articles.title: El líder de Superbike llega a MotoGP con el equipo de Rossi
articles.standfirst: Bulega, con una Ducati, en el VR46 desde 2027
articles.summary: Bulega, con una Ducati, en el VR46 desde 2027
articles.body: Son pocos, pero aún quedan algunos movimientos en el mercado de MotoGP 2027 por hacerse oficiales, porque todo está cerrado. Uno de ellos es el que ha hecho oficial el VR46, el equipo de Valentino Rossi, confirmando que Nicolò Bulega, el líder y casi campeón del Mundial de Superbike, correrá con ellos en 2027 y 2028. El italiano llega de la mano de Ducati, pues es, también su probador de la moto de 850cc y con el plus de haber llevado los neumáticos Pirelli estos últimos años. "Los de Superbike y Moto2 tendrán ventaja por eso", decía recientemente Pol Espargaró, piloto de pruebas de KTM y comentarista de DAZN. El transalpino tendrá como compañero en el box a otro piloto 'colocado' ahí por la fábrica de Borgo Panigale: Fermín Aldeguer. Sin duda, una dupla joven, pero con gran talento para optar cotas altas. Sustituirán a Fabio Di Giannantonio, que se va a KTM, y a Franco Morbidelli, que ocupará el lugar de Bulega en el conjunto oficial 'ducatista' en SBK. Nicolò fue alumno de la Academia y mostraba su entusiasmo por recalar ahí. "Llegar a MotoGP es un sueño, ya que debutaré con el Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team. Elegí este equipo porque siempre he estado vinculado a ellos: formé parte de la VR46 Riders Academy cuando era niño, así que conozco muy bien a todo el mundo. Por eso, dar este paso con gente conocida resulta más sencillo desde el punto de vista humano. Además, todos son extremadamente profesionales. Cuando empecé a competir, soñaba con llegar a MotoGP. Luego, por diversas razones, mi carrera tomó otro rumbo: pasé al WorldSBK, donde me centré en construir una trayectoria exitosa. Sin embargo, estos años han superado con creces mis expectativas, así que decidimos dar el salto a la categoría reina. Me alegra haber alcanzado esta meta, aunque haya tardado un poco más y haya seguido un camino distinto al habitual. Sin duda, es algo increíble y me siento muy orgulloso. Ahora no quiero fijarme objetivos concretos; quiero intentar hacerlo bien, ir carrera a carrera —especialmente al principio— y realizar el mejor trabajo posible. Quiero dar las gracias a todo el VR46 Racing Team, a Ducati Corse y a Aruba por hacerlo posible", decía. Uccio Salucci, el director del VR46, le augura éxitos. "Estamos encantados de dar la bienvenida a Nicolò al Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team. Le conocemos desde hace muchos años; comenzó su carrera con nosotros y juntos logramos grandes resultados. A lo largo del tiempo, tanto él como el equipo han crecido enormemente, y ahora estamos aquí para lograr grandes cosas juntos. Sabemos que es un piloto con mucho talento desde que era joven, algo que ha demostrado tanto en el pasado como en la actualidad dominando el WorldSBK. Creo que está preparado para emprender esta nueva etapa con madurez y plena conciencia. Estamos muy orgullosos de contar con él en nuestro equipo y le brindaremos el máximo apoyo posible para ayudarle a alcanzar todas sus metas. Gigi Dall'Igna, el CEO de Ducati Corse, igualmente espera mucho de su compatriota. "Estamos muy contentos de renovar nuestro acuerdo con Nicolò y de darle la bienvenida al proyecto de Ducati en MotoGP a partir de la próxima temporada. A lo largo de estos años, ha demostrado ser un piloto con gran talento, capaz de evolucionar constantemente, de sacar el máximo partido a nuestras motos y de alcanzar un nivel de competitividad extraordinario. Su trayectoria confirma que es un piloto con un presente sólido y exitoso, pero que al mismo tiempo posee un futuro muy prometedor. Creemos que ha llegado el momento adecuado para afrontar este nuevo desafío. El Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team es el entorno ideal para apoyarle durante su adaptación a MotoGP, y estamos convencidos de que contará con todas las herramientas necesarias para desarrollar su potencial al máximo. Este nuevo reto tendrá que esperar: por ahora, la prioridad sigue siendo el Campeonato del Mundo de Superbikes (WorldSBK). Nicolò está completando una gran temporada y es el momento de centrar todo el trabajo en un único objetivo: luchar juntos por el título mundial. Por último, quiero agradecer al equipo Aruba.it Racing – Ducati todo el trabajo realizado con Nicolò durante estas temporadas. Fueron los primeros en confiar en él, y el camino de crecimiento que le ha llevado a estar preparado para MotoGP es fruto de un compromiso compartido, del arduo trabajo del equipo y de la determinación que Nicolò ha demostrado año tras año.

articles.title: Red Bull ficha al hijo de Kimi Raikkonen de 11 años
articles.standfirst: Destaca en karts y para su equipo Júnior
articles.summary: Destaca en karts y para su equipo Júnior
articles.body: Red Bull ha hecho oficial la noticia que se gestó en Monza, durante el Gran Premio de Italia de F1: el fichaje de Robin Raikkonen, hijo de Kimi, para su programa de jóvenes pilotos, para el equipo júnior. En el trazado italiano ya se produjo una reunión en la que estuvieron el campeón de Fórmula 1 de 2007 con Gwen Lagrue, el responsable de contratar nuevos talentos, con Chalerm Yoovidhya y Oliver Mintzlaff, los nuevos grandes jefes de Red Bull. Todo porque Robin, a sus 11 años, ya ha despuntado en el mundo del kárting y varias marcas se lo estaban disputando. A sus 46 años, el antiguo piloto finlandés, ha visto el potencial de su vástago y le acompaña en todas sus competiciones, especialmente en Italia. Se da el caso de que 'Iceman', como el llamaban, sólo estuvo patrocinado por Red Bull... cuando se tomó un año sabático en el Gran Circo y se dedicó a los rallies. Gwen Lagrue, el artífice de este fichaje, se encarga del Red Bull Junior Team desde que Helmut Marko dejara estaba labor y la empresa. Antes trabajó en Mercedes y contrató a otro Kimi, Antonelli, quien ahora lidera con mano de hierro en F1 y está cerca de ganar su primer título.

articles.title: FIA: Ukraine automobile federation calls for sanctions on Russian counterpart
articles.summary: Ukraine's national motorsport authority calls on FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem to impose sanctions on its Russian counterpart for opening offices in occupied parts of Ukraine.
articles.body:
Ukraine's national motorsport authority has called on FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem to impose sanctions on its Russian counterpart.

The Russian automobile federation has opened offices in occupied parts of Ukraine in violation of the rules of the FIA, motorsport's governing body, according to the Ukraine federation (FAU).

The offices in Crimea, the city of Sevastopol and the Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia Oblasts are all located in areas recognised as sovereign Ukrainian territory by the United Nations.

The FAU's appeal for sanctions against its Russian counterpart (RAF) is the latest step it has made following the FIA's decision last month to lift the ban on Russian and Belarusian competitors in motorsport.

The FAU said in a statement that it was "outraged by the prolonged inaction of the global governing body".

It added: "The FAU has already appealed to the FIA senate and FIA ethics committee, but has received no reaction or reply."

It has also lodged a case with the FIA's international court of appeal.

FAU president Oleksander Feldman has written to Ben Sulayem demanding action.

He wrote: "Such short-sighted and counterproductive inaction is unbecoming of representatives of a global governing body. The current situation could have catastrophic consequences for the FIA's global standing.

"This is a dangerous precedent that paves the way for member organisations to disregard other provisions of the statutes and requirements of the rules, potentially leading to chaos and jeopardising the FIA's future as an institution."

Ukraine escalates protest over FIA lifting Russia ban

The FIA's rules permit only one automobile club or national sporting authority per country.

Feldman's letter demands that Ben Sulayem suspends Russia's membership, re-imposes "strict restrictions on Russian athletes' participation in international competitions", and makes a statement that publicly declares, on behalf of the FIA, that "the forcible redistribution of sporting authority is unacceptable".

The letter comes a week after Ukraine's minister for youth and sport told BBC Sport the FIA was wrong to lift the ban on Russian competitors.

Matvii Bidnyi said: "The reasons why Russia was banned from international sports competition have not disappeared. Nothing changes and it became even worse."

"Russia continues full-scale aggression against Ukraine. Belarus continues to provide military support to Russia. Ukrainian people are still being killed every day. And Russian attacks become more and more brutal.

"I don't understand, and Ukrainian people and I know that all European people don't understand what's happened, why now we must make this policy softer."

The ban on Russian and Belarusian competitors taking part in international motorsport events was imposed in February 2022, after Vladimir Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine.

It was lifted on 3 August in a decision by the FIA's world motorsport council. This followed the International Olympic Committee, with which the FIA is affiliated, lifting its own ban.

Other sporting authorities, such as World Athletics, have not followed suit.

The Russian Embassy in London said in a statement to BBC Sport last week: "Excluding Russian athletes from international competitions amounts to segregation based on nationality and is incompatible with the principles of the Olympic charter.

"The FIA's decision to lift the restrictions on Russian competitors in international motorsport is a step in the right direction. It shows that common sense is gradually prevailing over political bias in major sporting federations."

articles.body: Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of former Formula 1 world champion Kimi Raikkonen, has joined the Red Bull Junior Team. The young Finnish driver will enter Red Bull’s driver development programme from 2027 as he continues his early career in motorsport.Robin has already made a name for himself in karting. He currently sits second in the Rotax Max Challenge Italia standings. Red Bull believes he has shown impressive speed, racecraft and maturity for his age. The academy will now work with him and his family to develop his talent without putting unnecessary pressure on his young shoulders.Robin Raikkonen set to join Red Bull Junior Team from 2027Red Bull Racing Team Principal Laurent Mekies welcomed Robin Raikkonen to the programme and praised the youngster’s ability in karting.“Robin has already demonstrated exceptional ability in karting. His speed, racecraft and natural talent have established him as one of the most promising young drivers in his age group. At the same time, he impresses with his maturity, his calm approach and his clear focus on driving”, he said in a statement.“Our goal is to develop him step by step, without placing any unnecessary pressure on his shoulders. The path through motorsport is a long one, and we will give him the time, support and resources he needs to maximise his potential. We strongly believe that talent can thrive when supported by the right people, the right culture and the right environment”, he added.Notably, Robin has been involved in karting from a young age. His current second-place position in the Rotax Max Challenge Italia standings has further highlighted his potential.His arrival also adds another famous motorsport surname to Red Bull’s junior programme. The academy has produced some of Formula 1’s biggest stars, including four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel and four-time champion Max Verstappen.Robin’s father, Kimi Raikkonen, has a strong connection with Formula 1. Known around the world as ‘The Iceman’, he competed in F1 from 2001 to 2021.The Finn raced for teams including McLaren, Ferrari and Alfa Romeo. He won the 2007 F1 Drivers’ Championship with Ferrari. He also finished his career with 21 Grand Prix victories and 103 podium finishes.Kimi is now supporting his son’s journey into professional motorsport. He said the family is delighted with the opportunity.“We are all thrilled and excited that Robin has been chosen to further his racing path as a member of the Red Bull Junior Team. Laurent and everyone else at Red Bull have been incredibly supportive throughout all our discussions. Red Bull’s Junior Team has had years of incredible success. Its alumni include Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen amongst many others”, Kimi Raikkonen said in a statement.For now, Robin’s focus will remain on karting and gradual development. articles.title: Red Bull: Kimi Raikkonen's son Robin, 11, to join driver development programme
articles.summary: Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of former Formula 1 world champion Kimi Raikkonen, signs for Red Bull's driver development programme.
articles.body:
Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of former Formula 1 world champion Kimi Raikkonen, has signed for Red Bull.

Nicknamed 'Ace', the youngster has impressed in karting championships and will join Red Bull's driver development programme in 2027.

The programme has produced F1 drivers such as Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen - both four-time champions.

Robin's father, nicknamed 'Iceman', was the most recent Ferrari driver to become world champion, claiming his sole title in 2007.

The Finn claimed 21 wins and 103 podiums from 349 F1 starts before retiring in 2021. He also competed in the World Rally Championship and Nascar.

"We are all thrilled and excited that Robin has been chosen to further his racing path as a member of the Red Bull junior team," said 46-year-old Kimi.

"They offer a compelling and comprehensive programme to develop and nurture Robin's progress over the coming years and provide him with all the experience required to develop his natural talent."

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said Robin has "already demonstrated exceptional ability in karting".

"His speed, racecraft and natural talent have established him as one of the most promising young drivers in his age group," Mekies added.

"At the same time, he impresses with his maturity, his calm approach and his clear focus on driving.

"Our goal is to develop him step by step, without placing any unnecessary pressure on his shoulders.

"The path through motorsport is a long one and we will give him the time, support and resources he needs to maximise his potential."

Robin follows in the footsteps of Ella Hakkinen, the daughter of Finland's double world champion Mika Hakkinen, who joined McLaren's driver development programme last year.

articles.title: Verstappen sobre correr las 24 Horas de Le Mans con Alonso: "Lo hemos hablado"
articles.standfirst: En una entrevista con BBC, en holandés habla de una de sus ilusiones en el futuro y de tener al asturiano junto a él
articles.summary: En una entrevista con BBC, en holandés habla de una de sus ilusiones en el futuro y de tener al asturiano junto a él
articles.body: Max Verstappen es un enamorado de los GT, de la Resistencia y de casi cualquier coche de competición de elite del automovilismo. A Max le han preguntado directamente si es cierto que quiere correr Le Mans con Alonso, fue claro: "Lo hemos hablado". El piloto de Red Bull no oculta su admiración por el bicampeón mundial y destaca especialmente la gran experiencia de Alonso en carreras de resistencia como un valor añadido. "Miren a Fernando. Tiene 45 años y sigue yendo muy rápido. Para Le Mans, su experiencia podría ser una gran ventaja", ha señalado en una reciente entrevista en BBCx. Sin embargo, el plan futuro debe cumplir con condiciones estrictas. "Debe ajustarse a nuestros programas, tiene que tener sentido, debe ser bajo mis condiciones... Y debe haber una posibilidad real de vencer", dice sobre sus premisas irrenunciables. No sería correr por correr. Ya ha mostrado su predisposición hacia la resistencia, cuando este verano estuvo en las 24 Horas del Nürburgring, que calificó como "increíble correr una prueba así con mis compañeros. Una experiencia pura de motorsport", declaraba, aunque tampoco logró el triunfo en esa ocasión. Le Mans no es el único objetivo fuera de la Fórmula 1 para Verstappen. Ante la pregunta sobre otras carreras en sus planes, respondió sin dudar: "Todas las carreras de resistencia. Y por supuesto, tarde o temprano, los Hypercar. No quiero apresurarme, quiero hacerlo en el ambiente adecuado, bajo mis condiciones y siendo competitivo", reiteraba. Ahora viene la parte de los plazos. Recién renovado con Red Bull Hasta 2030, no sería al menos hasta 2031 el momento en el que podría dedicarle todo un año a un proyecto oficial y ganador del WEC, como Ferrari, Toyota, Peugeot... o Aston Martin, que podría ser el coche dentro de unos años. Fernando quizá podría quedar libre algo antes, en 2029, para volver al WEC con Aston y luego preparar el terreno para una posible llegada de Max con un Hypercar. Desde luego, sería la base de un equipo increíble, donde haría falta un tercer espada para completar el terceto obligado ahora en Le Mans.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes rather than Ferrari has taken pressure off Italian says Karun Chandhok
articles.summary: On the latest episode of Sky Sports F1's The F1 Show, Simon Lazenby, Karun Chandhok and David Croft discuss Kimi Antonelli's stunning win at Monza; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Antonelli joined the Mercedes junior programme as an 11-year-old after some remarkable results in karting and quickly rose up the motorsport ranks to Formula 1 and replaced Lewis Hamilton at the Silver Arrows only last year.

He currently leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from team-mate George Russell ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid and is on course to become the youngest world champion in F1 history at 20 years old.

His father, Marco Antonelli, has previously revealed he held discussions with Ferrari but the Scuderia did not want to sign someone so young whereas Mercedes were willing to take the risk.

On the latest episode of The F1 Show, Chandhok said: "I actually think by not making him a Ferrari junior, not putting him in front of Ferrari, not trying to make him a Ferrari young driver, and going down the Mercedes path, is actually the best thing that Marco Antonelli has done for his son. It's taken the pressure off in so many ways.

"Could you imagine if he was there as a Ferrari Italian driver? The pressure would be unbelievable. And Mercedes have done a fantastic job of nurturing him and bringing him here.

"I saw Kimi's parents and his sister afterwards by the Mercedes motorhome. They looked so delighted with the fact that obviously he'd won the home Grand Prix. I couldn't help but think they've managed to take away some pressure by not having him as a Ferrari driver."

Last week, Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes.

He said "as much as Ferrari is massive, incredible brand, I am very happy where I am" but Chandhok hopes he does drive in red one day.

"For the sake of the sport and the sake of Ferrari, I hope, a bit like Lewis, in 10, 15 years' time when Kimi's achieved a whole lot of things, maybe he will become a Ferrari driver. It'll be great for Ferrari to have him one day," he said.

Antonelli has stunned most of the F1 paddock this year with his speed and performances so far, but his most recent in Monza where he won from 19th on the grid made headlines around the world.

Sky Sports F1 's David Croft says Antonelli is a "generational talent" but is still "keeping his feet on the ground".

"At the start of the weekend he was getting pranked in the paddock, getting cream pies flung at him from his team as they got him back with a birthday surprise. I'm not sure the majority of F1 drivers on the grid would have stood for that," said Croft.

"Kimi absolutely revelled in it and there is a driver who is so at ease and so comfortable in the team that he's in. Long may that continue on track and off it as well. He is a total breath of fresh air for Formula 1."

Chandhok added: "He's been prepared from a much younger age as a professional, all-rounded driver - how to work with a team, how to work with a bigger structure.

"These kids now who are being signed to driver programmes from the ages of 10, 11, 12 in junior karting, they're being moulded from a younger age.

"You compare and contrast to the generation above, a Fernando Alonso or a Michael Schumacher, they only signed to professional contracts by the time they were already in F3.

"So I think, in some ways, it's not a surprise, I guess, that he is arriving as a more finished package because he's had 10 years of being as part of a professional structure, which the generation above wasn't."

articles.title: Marc Márquez, cauto: "En Misano será un poco más complicado"
articles.standfirst: Tras arrasar en MotorLand Aragón, el nueve veces campeón mundial adopta un perfil bajo en la antesala de la 14ª ronda del Mundial de MotoGP 2026
articles.summary: Tras arrasar en MotorLand Aragón, el nueve veces campeón mundial adopta un perfil bajo en la antesala de la 14ª ronda del Mundial de MotoGP 2026
articles.body: Vuelve el Mundial de MotoGP tras un breve receso. En MotorLand Aragón, Marc Márquez hizo bueno el pronóstico y logró un pleno de victorias (37 puntos de una tacada) que le aproximó al líder Jorge Martín. Con vistas a la cita de este fin de semana en Misano (14ª ronda del curso 2026), el de Aprilia aventaja en 19 puntos al nueve veces campeón (256 frente a 237). Y eso es una excelente noticia para el '93' porque, como ha admitido Claudio Domenicali, CEO de Ducati, ese escenario era impensable tras la caída en el Sprint de Le Mans. “Hace tres meses, este Campeonato del Mundo parecía irremediablemente perdido. Hoy, el panorama es muy diferente, y diría que el campeonato está completamente abierto”, ha expuesto el mandamás en La Gazzetta dello Sport. En este contexto, el gran premio que se va a disputa del 11 al 13 de septiembre en el Circuito Marco Simoncelli es una prueba clave por que aquí es difícil vislumbrar qué nivel puede ofrecer el '93'. Al manillar de una Ducati, Marc se impuso en esta pista tanto en 2024 como en 2025. Como exponen los datos estadísticos es un trazado en el que ha conseguido buenos resultados, pero que no es de sus favoritos. Aparte está el factor de que aquí abundan los hinchas de Ducati... pero también hay mucho fan de Valentino Rossi. "En Aragón conseguimos el máximo de puntos posibles y ese era nuestro objetivo. MotorLand es un circuito que se adapta muy bien a mi estilo de pilotaje. Aquí, en Misano, será un poco más complicado, pero sigue siendo una pista donde puedo intentar rendir al máximo y llevar la Desmosedici GP al límite de su potencial", pormenoriza el competidor de Cervera en unas declaraciones proporcionadas por la firma de Borgo Panigale. Finalmente, el ganador de 103 carreras (amén de 169 podios y 105 poles) recalca la importancia de correr en un territorio con mucho tifosi de su escudería. "Habrá muchísimos aficionados de Ducati, y eso siempre puede darte ese extra que marca la diferencia", cierra el '93'.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Owen Burrows’ filly can claim Park Hill success
articles.summary: Our ambassador previews a busy Thursday on Town Moor which features the Group Two Park Hill Stakes – live on Sky Sports Racing from 1.15pm
articles.body:
The race they call the Fillies' Leger, the Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes (3.00), is one of the highlights of the opening day of the Betfred St Leger Festival at Doncaster on Thursday and I expect a competitive renewal to go the way of the Owen Burrows-trained Waardah .

She has run two big races in a light campaign in pattern company this year, including in the Group Two Lillie Langtry Stakes at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, only to pay the price for a touch of freshness early in the race - her first since May.

With a hood fitted for the first time, she can prove too good for some classy types including Fairy Glen who shone out in Meydan in the spring when taking the Dubai Gold Cup over two miles from Friday's probable Doncaster Cup favourite Caballo De Mar.

Simon and Ed Crisford's mare has proven form on the back of a break so shouldn't be troubled by a four-month absence and her stamina beyond this extended mile-and-three-quarter trip is assured.

Godolphin's filly Musical Times brings a burgeoning reputation to the other Group Two on the opening day at Doncaster, the Betfred May Hill Stakes (3.35) for the two-year-olds.

Unbeaten in novice races at Newmarket and Yarmouth and on course for a possible crack at the Group One Fillies' Mile, this exciting daughter of Lope De Vega is a fascinating runner in this recognised Classic trial.

However, she hasn't beaten a lot at this stage so I'm taking her on with Irish raider Sea Of Rain , who has already proven herself at a high level with victory in a Group Three at the Curragh last time. Jim Bolger's filly has plenty of experience and won't mind a bit of cut in the ground.

Can't see past Vegas in valuable sales race

I just can't see past the likely favourite Night In Vegas in the big juvenile cavalry charge on the opening day, the Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes (1.50).

Eve Johnson Houghton's colt boasts a lofty rating of 102 yet gets a considerable amount of weight from many of his closest rivals under the terms of this race. His credentials are impeccable with a valuable auction race success at Newmarket last time coming on the back of a creditable third in the Group Two Richmond Stakes at the Goodwood Festival.

I'm hoping to see my husband Tom (Marquand) go well on William Haggas's God Given Talent who was unlucky in running when fourth in a hot nursery at York's Ebor Festival on his first start for the yards since leaving James Ferguson.

Satellite Of Love , who like God Given Talent has a rating of 91, can also play a part. Clive Cox's colt was unbeaten in his first two starts before finishing a well beaten fifth behind the thrown-in Group One winner Sun Goddess in that York sales race.

Cox filly can make winning nursery debut

Art Of Life is yet to get her head in front but can make a winning debut out of novice company in the British Stallion Studs 'Carrie Red' EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap (1.15) on Thursday.

Cox's filly has been unlucky to bump into a couple of promising types at Newbury, including when a shade too keen behind Tom's hot favourite Sweetwonderfulyou last time.

I marginally prefer her to Richard Spencer's likely favourite Speed Of Sound , a lovely Sioux Nation filly who ran a stormer at the weights behind Sun Goddess in that valuable sales race at York.

At a much bigger price, Richard Hannon's Rollthedicebaby has the talent to get back on track off an easing mark after finishing in the pack behind Speed Of Sound on the Knavesmire.

Tom and his boss William have the one they all have to beat in the mile and a quarter Pertemps Network Handicap (2.25) on the opening day.

King Of Earth impressed me when taking a valuable Curragh handicap in the summer in first time cheekpieces and can be forgiven his effort last time in Group Three company at York.

Back in a handicap with the ground and a good draw in his favour, he can get quickly back on track at the possible expense of John and Thady Gosden's Runman .

It's early days for the son of Frankel who put a two-month break behind him to win over this trip at Newbury last time. He looks very well treated off just a three-pound higher mark and will enjoy conditions on Town Moor.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Watch every race of the Betfred St Leger Festival live on Sky Sports Racing (Sky 415 | Virgin 512) from Thursday 10th to Sunday 13th September.

articles.title: Alonso pasa por el Circuit antes de llegar a Madring
articles.summary: Fernando Alonso ha hecho una parada este miércoles en Montmeló, en su viaje de Mónaco a Madrid, donde este fin de semana le espera el GP de España de F1 en su regreso a la capital de España.
articles.body: Fernando Alonso ha hecho una parada este miércoles en Montmeló, en su viaje de Mónaco a Madrid, donde este fin de semana le espera el GP de España de F1 en su regreso a la capital de España. El piloto de Aston Martin lo anunciaba esta mañana, "uno de los mejores días del año. Juguetes + Barcelona", decía en su cuenta oficial de Instagram, para indicar que se trataba de una jornada privada de pruebas. Fernando es embajador del Circuit de Barcelona desde 2025 y suele organizar jornadas de 'hot laps' con varios GT de su propiedad, pero esta vez se trataba de otra cosa. Poco después colgaba otra foto de un McLaren MP4/4 de 1988, con el que Senna ganó uno de sus títulos y luego un vídeo sobre otro McLaren, esta vez el suyo de 2007, de la famosa temporada en la que empató a puntos con Hamilton, quizá la más recordada junto con el reciente 2021. Este jueves, Fernando estará en la rueda de prensa oficial de la FIA en Madring, donde también intervendrá Carlos Sainz, pero antes tuvo la ocasión de desquitarse de tanta recarga y tanto deployment de energía como exigen los monoplazas de 2026 y que tan poco agradan a los pilotos. El público sí se está divirtiendo con remontadas como la de Antonelli el pasado domingo en Monza y las alternativas y adelantamientos que hay en pista en casi todas las carreras. Sólo hay que ver su story con un violín, en un pequeño vídeo de Alonso pilotando aquel McLaren Vodafone, que todos los aficionados recuerdan y él añora con su V8 y sin baterías.

articles.summary: Rinde homenaje al coche con el que se proclamaron campeones del mundo de constructores en el Circuito del Jarama en 1981
articles.body: Williams ha querido rendir tributo a su glorioso pasado con la decoración que va a presentar en el Gran Premio de España de Fórmula 1 que se disputa desde el 11 al 13 de septiembre en el flamante Madring. Carlos Sainz, que se puede afirmar sin tapujos que corre en su casa, tendrá a su disposición un FW48 con un look especial, amén de que llevará un casco exclusivo diseñado para esta histórica ocasión. La escudería de Grove ha considerado oportuno que el '55' y Alex Albon estén a los mandos de un monoplaza que rinde tributo al FW07C (pilotado por Alan Jones y Carlos Reutemann) que compitió en el Circuito del Jarama en 1981, el coche con el que Williams se proclamó campeón mundial de constructores aquel año. El blanco, el verde y el azul marino eran los colores de aquel coche que ahora han resucitado con motivo de la cita madrileña. "Nuestro objetivo de volver al frente de la parrilla está inspirado en todo lo que hemos hecho antes. Estoy increíblemente orgulloso de celebrarlo con la decoración especial de Atlassian, conectando el equipo que éramos en el Jarama con el equipo en el que nos estamos convirtiendo hoy. El coche tiene un aspecto fantástico y estoy deseando verlo dando vueltas por Madrid", ha expuesto James Vowles, jefe de equipo de Williams.

articles.title: Piloto questiona rota e ouve provocação durante voo com destino a MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Piloto disse que alteração poderia impactar autonomia e segurança do voo, que tinha Varginha como destino; frase foi dita por uma voz ainda não identificada durante a transmissão de rádio.
articles.summary: Piloto disse que alteração poderia impactar autonomia e segurança do voo, que tinha Varginha como destino; frase foi dita por uma voz ainda não identificada durante a transmissão.
articles.body:
Um piloto que seguia do Rio de Janeiro para Minas Gerais questionou uma mudança de rota determinada pelo controle de tráfego aéreo e ouviu, durante a comunicação por rádio, uma frase em tom de provocação: “Amigão, você não manda nem em casa, quer mandar aqui”.

O caso aconteceu no dia 4 de setembro, durante um voo de um Cessna 525 CitationJet M2, de matrícula PS-KCI, que tinha Varginha (MG) como destino. Segundo o piloto Pedro Costa, de 35 anos, havia três pessoas a bordo da aeronave: ele, o copiloto e um passageiro.

A autoria do comentário ainda não foi identificada. Segundo Pedro, a frase não foi dita pela controladora com quem ele mantinha a comunicação e ocorreu em meio a uma discussão sobre uma mudança na rota.

Piloto questiona rota e ouve provocação durante voo com destino a MG — Foto: Maurício Costa Spotter

Pedro contou ao g1 que a intenção inicial era sair do Aeroporto de Jacarepaguá, no Rio de Janeiro, com destino a Varginha.

Segundo ele, a configuração inicial não foi aprovada por causa da existência de uma área militar ativa no trajeto. Para que o plano de voo fosse aceito, foi necessário contornar o espaço aéreo restrito.

Já durante o voo, segundo Pedro, o controle informou que seria necessária uma nova alteração, desta vez com a orientação para que a aeronave prosseguisse pelo fixo MUDKA.

“Essa alteração representaria um acréscimo significativo de milhas à rota previamente planejada e aprovada, conduzindo inicialmente a aeronave em direção oposta ao destino pretendido”, afirmou.

🔎 PIRAÍ, NIGMA e MUDKA, siglas citadas no áudio, são pontos de navegação (waypoints) usados para definir rotas no espaço aéreo.

Pedro afirmou ainda que a solicitação para que a aeronave fizesse um desvio para a direita foi justificada pelo controle como uma forma de evitar conflito com outra aeronave. O piloto alega, porém, que tanto o radar utilizado por ele durante o voo quanto os registros disponíveis em um site de rastreamento de aeronaves não indicariam a presença de outra aeronave na região que justificasse o desvio solicitado.

Diante da mudança, o piloto, que afirmou ter 14 anos de experiência na função, disse ter informado ao órgão de controle que o desvio poderia afetar o planejamento operacional, principalmente em relação ao combustível e à autonomia da aeronave.

“Identifiquei a necessidade de informar prontamente ao controle que não seria possível cumprir aquela alteração, uma vez que o desvio proposto impactaria diretamente o planejamento realizado, especialmente em relação à autonomia, combustível disponível e segurança operacional do voo”, explicou.

Pedro afirmou, no entanto, que não se recusou a seguir as orientações do controle, mas pediu uma alternativa que evitasse o desvio em direção oposta a Varginha.

Pedro Costa tem 35 anos, 14 deles como piloto — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Pedro Costa

Controladora explicou motivo da alteração

Segundo o piloto, a controladora informou que a mudança estava relacionada ao sequenciamento do tráfego aéreo, com outras aeronaves descendo em sentido contrário, em direção ao Aeroporto Internacional do Galeão, no Rio de Janeiro.

Pedro afirmou que a comunicação com a controladora ocorreu de maneira cordial e que ela explicou o motivo da alteração.

“A profissional mostrou-se solícita, compreendeu a preocupação apresentada e explicou de forma clara a dimensão da alteração, sua motivação e que se tratava de uma medida destinada à organização do fluxo de tráfego aéreo”, afirmou.

O piloto também ressaltou que, em nenhum momento, houve oposição ao cumprimento das orientações recebidas.

“A aeronave foi conduzida conforme a instrução recebida e, posteriormente, após a coordenação com o órgão, foi possível obter uma alteração de rota mais compatível com o planejamento e a autonomia disponível”, disse.

Após os questionamentos, a rota acabou sendo encurtada, conforme registros disponíveis em aplicativos de rastreamento de voos, e a aeronave seguiu em direção ao destino.

Foi durante essa comunicação que uma voz fez o comentário: “Amigão, você não manda nem em casa, quer mandar aqui”.

Para Pedro, a comunicação entre pilotos e controladores deve ser objetiva e voltada para questões operacionais.

“Comentários pessoais, ironias ou manifestações estranhas à operação não contribuem para a comunicação efetiva em frequência e podem interferir desnecessariamente na fonia, especialmente considerando que a mesma frequência pode estar sendo utilizada por aeronaves que necessitem transmitir informações relevantes, solicitar auxílio ou comunicar situações de urgência ou emergência”, afirmou.

Pedro disse ainda que considera importante que o episódio seja analisado sob a perspectiva da segurança operacional. Ele foi orientado a registrar a mudança de rota por meio de um Relatório de Prevenção (RELPREV), junto à Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac). Segundo ele, o comentário feito durante a comunicação por rádio também foi incluído no relato.

Trecho de comunicação circulou nas redes

O áudio veio a público por meio de Thamiris dos Passos, de 24 anos, que mora em Itaguaí, na Região Metropolitana do Rio de Janeiro. Entusiasta da aviação, ela contou ao g1 que costuma acompanhar transmissões de comunicação entre pilotos e órgãos de controle.

“Eu já entendo como é a comunicação normalmente entre os pilotos e as torres dos aeroportos, mas essa que ocorreu eu verifiquei que não se tratava de uma comunicação normal, como de autorização de pouso ou decolagem, e sim de rota”, contou.

Segundo Thamiris, a conversa chamou a atenção porque estava mais informal do que as comunicações técnicas que costuma acompanhar.

Ela enviou o áudio para uma página especializada em aviação no Instagram. “Decidi não apenas deixar passar, pois era algo que poderia ser necessário ser divulgado para algo importante”, afirmou.

Thamiris dos Passos tem 24 anos e é entusiasta da aviação — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Thamiris dos Passos

Thamiris também disse que tentou entrar em contato com o piloto Pedro Costa depois que ele apareceu nos comentários da publicação sobre o caso, mas ainda não conseguiu falar diretamente com ele.

Ela afirmou que considera que o piloto fez corretamente ao questionar a alteração da rota.

“Eu concordo com ele em ter perguntado sobre a rota e tentar compreender o porquê foi mudada após a criação que ele fez do plano de voo. Mesmo estando certo ou errado, eu concordo em verificar, confirmar e perguntar à controladora”, disse.

Além de ser entusiasta da área, a jovem contou que pretende fazer o curso para comissária de bordo e tentar ingressar na Aeronáutica.

O g1 entrou em contato com o Departamento de Controle do Espaço Aéreo (Decea), órgão responsável pelo monitoramento e controle do tráfego aéreo em território brasileiro, para esclarecer a alteração da rota e o comentário feito durante a comunicação por rádio, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Tunisian flotilla activists remain jailed as hunger striker worsens
articles.summary: The four have been held since March in a financial investigation linked to organisers of the Global Sumud Flotilla.
articles.body:
Tunis, Tunisia – Six months after Tunisian authorities began arresting organisers of a pro-Palestinian flotilla, four activists remain in pre-trial detention, with growing concern over the health of one of them, who has been on hunger strike for more than three weeks.

Wael Naouar, a Tunisian activist and member of the steering committee of the Global Sumud Flotilla, began his hunger strike on August 16 to protest his continued detention.

His lawyer, Bassem Trifi, who is also president of the Tunisian League for Human Rights (LTDH), said on Tuesday that Naouar was entering his 24th day without food and described his condition as “very serious”.

Trifi, who visited Naouar in prison last week, said the activist had lost 18kg (40lb) and was suffering from low blood pressure and low blood sugar, as well as difficulty breathing, walking and speaking. He was also experiencing pain throughout his body, particularly in his stomach, Trifi said.

Anis Harrathi, an activist and member of the committee supporting the detainees, said Naouar was aware of the physical risks of a prolonged hunger strike, but had chosen to continue because he believed remaining silent was more perilous than continuing his strike.

“Wael knows very well the risks of a hunger strike,” Harrathi told Al Jazeera. “Yet he chose to put his body in confrontation with an entire system, because there comes a moment when silence becomes more dangerous than hunger.”

Harrathi said Naouar’s protest was not about personal heroism but what he sees as a broader injustice affecting him and the other detainees.

“Wael is not protesting only against his imprisonment,” Harrathi said. “He is protesting against a logic that wants to turn prison into a tool used to silence opposing voices, turn solidarity with Palestine into a charge, and turn civil and political activism into a security case.”

Seven activists were initially detained in connection with the investigation in March. Three have since been released, leaving Naouar and three others, Nabil Channoufi, Ghassan Henchiri and Ghassan Boughdiri, in pre-trial detention.

The case remains under judicial investigation, and none of the four has been convicted of an offence.

The investigation was ordered by Tunisia’s Economic and Financial Judicial Pole, a specialised body that handles major economic and financial cases, over what state news agency TAP described, citing a judicial source, as “suspicious financial flows” received by organisers of the Global Sumud Flotilla.

Investigators have been examining the origin and use of the funds and whether they were diverted for purposes unrelated to the flotilla.

Trifi said the investigation concerns allegations including money laundering, aggravated breach of trust, and forgery. He argued that the fundraising activities at the centre of the case were part of a solidarity campaign and should not be treated in the same way as ordinary financial transactions subject to public procurement and accounting rules.

He also said the fundraising took place at a known location “under the protection of the security services and under the eyes of the state”.

Tunisian authorities have not publicly detailed the allegations against the four or responded to requests for comment on their detention and Naouar’s health.

Supporters of the detainees reject the allegations and say the case is aimed at criminalising solidarity with Palestinians and efforts to organise another flotilla towards Gaza. The Global Sumud Flotilla has described the allegations as unfounded and called for the activists’ release.

“What is happening to him [Naouar] and the other detainees cannot be treated as simply a separate judicial case detached from its political context,” Harrathi told Al Jazeera.

The case comes amid growing international criticism of Tunisia’s treatment of civil society groups and activists.

A Human Rights Watch report published last week documented what it described as the “weaponisation” of financial and criminal investigations, alongside arrests, detention and administrative measures, against civil society organisations and their members in the country. The group said at least 47 people connected to NGOs in Tunisia had been prosecuted and at least 14 convicted and sentenced to prison since 2025.

Human Rights Watch said authorities had used financial crime and money-laundering laws against human rights defenders and NGO workers, raising concerns that such investigations were being used to intimidate and restrict civic space.

Meanwhile, Rachid Othmani, a member of the National Committee for Defense of Sumud Flotilla Activists, spoke at a solidarity rally in Tunis on Sunday, saying supporters would not be intimidated by prison or repression and would continue their campaign until the detainees were freed.

“Our eyes and hearts are with our comrade Wael, who is standing firm in the face of death,” Othmani said. “His life and his legacy will be longer and greater than those of those holding him.”

Brazilian activist Thiago Avila, who took part in the flotilla and was previously detained by Israel, has also called for the Tunisian activists to be released, saying no one should be detained for acting in solidarity with Palestinians.

The human rights group HuMENA has also called for their release, saying the continued pre-trial detention raises concerns over due process and the criminalisation of peaceful civic activity.

The arrests have unfolded amid growing restrictions on civil society and political activity in Tunisia under President Kais Saied.

Saied has consolidated power across state institutions since 2021, when he suspended parliament, dismissed the government, and began ruling by decree. His government has faced sustained criticism from rights groups, which accuse authorities of using prosecutions and prolonged pre-trial detention against political opponents, journalists, lawyers and activists.

Saied and his government have rejected accusations that prosecutions are politically motivated and have maintained that the judiciary operates independently.

The four activists are due to appear in court on September 16, and Naouar’s hunger strike is now entering its fourth week.

Despite his deteriorating health, Trifi said Naouar remains determined to continue his hunger strike. When asked how far he thought Naouar was prepared to take it, Trifi pointed to a phrase the activist often tells his wife when he is detained: “Until the stars burn out.”

articles.title: Spanish Grand Prix 2026: Can football-obsessed Madrid embrace F1?
articles.summary: After F1’s explosion in popularity away from its European heartland the sport is coming home. Why Madrid? Because it is beautiful… and has a very big expo centre on the outskirts.
articles.body:
You could never accuse Formula 1 of shirking a challenge.

Who else would consider competing for the attention of a football-obsessed country, home to the World Cup winners, in a city where a constant stream of the world's most talented players do awe-inspiring things most weeks?

F1 last had a Spanish world champion 20 years ago and there hasn't been a race in Madrid since 1981.

Does F1, which has experienced a huge rise in popularity in other territories around the world, need another track in its crowded European heartland?

This weekend the sport, and Madrid itself, will find out.

Real Madrid are considered to be the greatest football club in history.

They have won 15 European Cups and 36 La Liga titles, and then there are the famous Galacticos: the generational set of the world's best players which began with the likes of Zinedine Zidane and Ronaldo and has extended to the modern crop that includes Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe.

Some 75,000 Madridistas roared home Mbappe's majestically deft volley to make it 3-0 after half an hour against Malaga at the end of August, and their city rivals Atletico aren't far adrift of them in La Liga. It's hard to see what else the locals need to sate their sporting needs.

But in both the stunning, newly reconditioned steel spaceship of the Bernabeu, which has lost none of the drama of its frighteningly steep theatrical terracing, or Real Madrid women's atmospheric if less salubrious stadium right next to the new F1 track, will fans be turning their attention to the roar of the engine noise this weekend?

"Yes, [the F1 race] is good for Madrid," says one. "There is pride in our sport, Madrid is an open city with open people and open minds.

"The race can [take] Madrid's [identity] outside of football, and the most we can be seen [by the outside world] is the best.

"But I'm more than excited… I'm curious - I want to see how it goes."

"We've always been dreaming of having something [from F1] closer to home," adds another. "Having it back is great. I've been to Barcelona and the Belgian GP and I think let's see how it goes. Organising tends to be messy in the first year - I don't want to be the guinea pig.

"Let's hope it brings the city more into the spotlight. Madrid has a lot to learn from F1 about how to run a global spectacle; F1 could probably learn the true Spanish way. Barcelona is more international, the drivers and fans coming to Madrid will get more of a taste of Spain."

As the Prado museum demonstrates, Madrid knows its fine art.

The crossing signals resemble birdsong and the Mexican conifers gently sway over the waiting traffic with a backdrop of stunning Palaciosian architecture, which is in contrast to the relatively flat, block layout of the inner city.

This may not have made for the best race experience so instead, organisers plumped for what outsiders may see as an unloved expo area run by the quasi-state owned Ifema organisation next to the city's airport.

"It started as a joke, it was a fantasy," says Luis Garcia Abad, Madring boss and former manager to Spain's only world champion Fernando Alonso, among other Spanish sports stars.

"An F1 grand prix is like a unicorn - you are trying always to see the unicorn but at the end you realise [sometimes] it's impossible.

"The queue of cities trying to organise an F1 GP is huge. They have to choose right - we signed a contract for 10 years.

"Maybe seven or eight years ago we talked about this race. At some point Ifema called me and said 'what are you thinking [about its viability]?' After one morning [here] I said: 'It's possible.'

The new venue may be a world away from the flamenco-inspired boutiques and wine bars of the intimate Salamanca district, but Madrid is relatively diminutive compared to other high-profile capitals, and has high-quality public transport.

As a result, organisers are cutting out many of the car parks and asking fans to leave their own motors at home.

But don't expect Patrick Dempsey, Rafael Nadal and Mbappe to be standing on the platform of Avenida de America to hop on the pink line to the circuit – they will breathe easy at the VIP spaces near to the expansive six-strong VIP area paddock.

Regardless of the journey there, what will fans find?

"It's a real experience, not just to be in Madrid but for F1," says Abad. "Every part of the track has its own personality. Monumental… Turn 12, is huge, amazing.

"We really wanted to have an iconic part of the circuit – more than 30,000 people around one corner."

Ah yes, Monumental. The corner everyone in F1 is talking about when discussing this race.

A 26-degree banked challenge, substantially longer than the one at the Dutch Grand Prix's Zandvoort. Monumental scythes through what will feel like a small town come race day.

It comes complete with a VIP viewing area that could house the King of Spain and his family and sits, appropriately, like a castle on top of the hill. It's a difficult structure to walk up, and in 44C heat, impossible to sit on.

"Luis wanted to think of something recognisable in our circuit. Something iconic," says operations director for Ifema Carlos Jimenez.

Monumental was not the only complex part of a track build, which Jimenez says lends itself to sustainability. Power for the race comes from renewable energy and there is partial use of existing buildings around the site. However, additional construction around the circuit has seen 65m euros of investment, and the track itself cost 85m euros alone.

"There were a lot of challenges," he says. "We started building it in the wettest winter in 20 years in Spain. The rain was torrential. We suffered a lot, and had to stabilise parts of clay which behaves badly with wet conditions. It was very challenging. There are three layers of asphalt here. We learnt from one layer to the next.

"In 2022 it seemed like a little bit of a crazy idea," adds Jimenez. "But Madrid has momentum right now; it's a vibrant city, very well known for football.

"Like a ski resort must have entertainment for apres-ski, a circuit must have good after-race entertainment. Madrid will become in top position - the offer of this city is incredible in terms of gastronomy, a spectacular climate, which is very mild in September. And the party in Madrid is unbeatable."

Make no mistake, Madring is a street circuit: part public roads, part purpose built. And it feels intense to stand on the track, let alone drive it, with the walls on either side appearing to close in on you. And that lack of width, on the eye at least, suggests overtaking will be virtually impossible.

"From a driver's point of view it's quite a harsh circuit," says an excited Abad. "Twenty-two corners, up and down, banking corners - the circuit is adapted to the new [F1] regulations.

"I spoke with Charles Leclerc and he said it was an amazing track, and in the race I believe you will have the opportunity to overtake, but not by free. We're talking about gladiators – the best drivers in the world."

Plenty of drivers have already experienced Madring in anger during a Formula 3 test.

"It's going to be really edgy," says Madrid's own F3 driver Bruno del Pino. "You are always on the limit, the corners are quick and the walls are close. It's like [Saudi GP circuit] Jeddah but with more difficulty.

"With Monumental, you see so much of an angle it never ends. The first time around, you see it going straight up and you feel like you'll fly straight out [of the track].

"It is flat for us because of the downforce so it's not really a corner, but the previous combination of Turns 10 and 11 are high speed and close to the wall - quite a few drivers will kiss the wall."

Britain's F3 driver Freddie Slater goes even further: "A lap of Madrid is so exhilarating, and the adrenaline is pumping - it's an incredible track to drive. It's one of the best tracks on calendar, if not the best.

"It's got character, it's got bumps, uphill and downhill – it's a bit more old-school."

Abad believes it's the spectators who will determine this race's success.

"Not just Madrid needing F1, maybe even F1 needing Madrid," he concludes. "We're investing money to create an experience inside of a city.

"The future of the [F1] championship is something in this direction – we need to take care of customers and spectators. They are our future."

articles.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Leger meeting at Doncaster kicks off with Park Hill and May Hill clashes
articles.summary: Watch every race from all four days of Doncaster's St Leger meeting, including Saturday's Classic clash, all live on Sky Sports Racing; Lingfield, Worcester and ParisLongchamp also in action on Thursday
articles.body:
3.00 Doncaster - Consent and Danielle headline strong field

A top-class field has assembled for the Group Two Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes where Consent and Danielle feature among nine runners.

Danielle, fourth in this contest last year, ended the campaign with an emphatic nine-length win in Listed company here in November. A winner of the Bronte Cup on her return this season, she disappointed at Goodwood and will be hoping to bounce back under William Buick.

Consent finished a neck second in this race last season before landing Group One honours in the Prix de Royallieu. She has struggled to match those highs since and connections reach for the cheekpieces.

Andrew Balding's Prizeland took the Galtres Stakes at York with plenty to spare and rates an each-way player, while Waardah will enjoy any easing of the ground. She finished ahead of the top pair at Goodwood and must be feared if able to repeat the feat in a first-time hood.

Fairy Glen was only beaten half a length in the Prix Vicomtesse Vigier in May and would have claims if fit enough on her return.

3.35 Doncaster - Unbeaten Musical Times heads up in grade

Unbeaten Musical Times heads up in grade for this Group Two Betfred May Hill Stakes.

The Charlie Appleby-trained filly arrives having impressed on both starts to date and tops the betting under William Buick. Having outpointed the reopposing Scommessa Sicura on her debut at Newmarket, she oozes quality when landing the odds at Yarmouth and deserves a crack at this better contest.

Scommessa Sicura has finished in the top two on her five starts to date and produced a career-best when second a Salisbury last month.

Joseph O'Brien saddles Ballyskeagh who ran a huge race to finish runner-up in a Group Three at Curragh over the mile and that gives her solid place claims, while Speckles was fifth that day and may improve again.

1.50 Doncaster - Night In Vegas spearheads big field

All eyes will be on Night In Vegas as he bids to plunge another huge pot in this Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes.

Eve Johnson Houghton's colt sets the standard having finished fifth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot before landing the £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes on his last start. That entitles him to be a short-priced favourite, and he is weighted to go close.

Plenty have chances including George Boughey's Shadwell colt Mithaaly . He stepped up on his first two starts to win comfortably at Windsor and should be monitored in the market.

Zigazig Ah took the Weatherbys Super Sprint at Newbury back in July before failing to fire at Goodwood. She chased home Night In Vegas at Newmarket and looks capable of better.

Joseph O'Brien's experienced Seven Nation Army completes the shortlist.

The Sky Sports Racing cameras also head to Lingfield and Worcester. Marquessofanglesey has hit the crossbar a few times now and may make that experience finally count at Lingield (3.15) under Rob Hornby.

Over at Worcester, Harry Cobden gets aboard former Cheltenham Festival runner-up Crebilly , taking on hat-trick seeker Youdecide and Snipe for the Skelton team (2.10).

There is British interest at ParisLongchamp in the Group Three Prix Gladiateur as Midak represents Ian Williams, taking on former Group One winner Double Major .

articles.standfirst: Sólo queda una parte de los 'hospitalities' VIP más exclusivos
articles.summary: Sólo queda una parte de los 'hospitalities' VIP más exclusivos
articles.body: Las algo más de 100.000 entradas generales de Madring están completamente vendidas desde el miércoles. Las gradas del trazado estarán repletas para un público que ha pagado entre los 265 euros de la pelousse (de pie) y los 1.500 euros de la recta principal, según informó ayer la organización de Ifema. Las únicas plazas disponibles, son la VIP, que van desde los 800 euros (aún con plazas en el Mirador de la Monumental), hasta los 2.500 euros, con experiencia gastronómica premium y suites reducidas, pero muchas de ellas están a punto de agotarse también, por lo que la entrada de 135.000 personas el domingo y unas 350.000 a lo largo del fin de semana, van a ser una realidad. Todo estará completo para la primera edición de una carrera que puede convertirse en en clásico en Europa, como ha sucedido con Miami en los últimos años en Estados Unidos, gracias a otro concepto de F1. La peligrosidad y exigencia del circuito preceden a este escenario antes de empezar, aunque luego, con los coches en pista puede ser diferente. "En Bakú, el primer año, íbamos todos en fila india y no pasó nada, por ese respeto inicial", recuerda Carlos Sainz, que no está muy seguro hacia dónde romperán el fin de semana ni el nuevo trazado.

articles.title: Jesús Calleja avala a Cristina Gutiérrez: "Habría cambiado correr yo para que lo hiciera ella"
articles.standfirst: "Es una mujer que puede hacer cosas increíbles", asegura el leónes, que propuso su fichaje
articles.summary: "Es una mujer que puede hacer cosas increíbles", asegura el leónes, que propuso su fichaje
articles.body: La carrera deportiva de Cristina Gutiérrez no se va a quedar colgada después de que Dacia decidiera cerrar su proyecto Dakar de forma anticipada. La piloto burgalesa, ganadora del Dakar 2026 en la categoría Challenger, seguirá siendo una de las protagonistas de la clase reina de los raids, esta vez luciendo los colores de una marca española, Santana. Y uno de los que más han apostado por ese fichaje ha sido el asesor deportivo de la firma de Linares, el aventurero y presentador Jesús Calleja. El leonés, que estrenó el coche español en el Dakar 2026 (con poca fortuna ya que acabó destrozado en un accidente), contó a MARCA cuál fue su papel en la decisión de apostar por Gutiérrez. "Este año estaba todo raro para ella. Se quedaba sin coche, no veía yo que hubiese alguna estructura potente que fuese a apostar por ella y hablé con Edu Blanco, el CEO, y el equipo de Santana y les dije: ¿Cómo no fichamos a Cristina, si es lo mejor? No va a haber nadie mejor que ella como piloto, como persona, como alguien que represente a la marca en la competición", explica. La propuesta, en su calidad de asesor del Santana Racing Team, fue muy bien recibida y, de hecho, los directivos se pusieron a ello y ha acabado cuajando el fichaje: "Fue increíble porque a todos les pareció estupendo. Santana tienen un gran equipo detrás, funciona como una familia, y en seguida se puso la maquinaria en marcha para ofrcerle el mejor coche posible". El fichaje de Cristina Gutiérrez pone el proyecto de Santana en los raids en una dimensión superior. "Con Cristina se ha hecho un esfuerzo enorme porque Santana aún es una marca que está empezando, pero esto demuestra las ganas que tiene de seguir adelante, porque fíjate qué fichaje". "Es una apuesta a largo plazo, para que se identifique con la marca y pueda trabajar a fondo con el coche. Cristina es muy buena desarrollando coches y ella lo va a hacer extraordinario. Además, se va a preparar bien, haciendo test, corriendo... va a haber unos años muy exitosos con Cristina". Desde el punto de vista personal de Calleja, su apoyo a Cristina Gutiérrez va más allá de lo deportivo: "Yo con Cristina tengo una amistad extraordinaria, pero sobre todo tengo la visión de que es una mujer que puede hacer cosas increíbles. Puede estar arriba con cualquiera si las condiciones son favorables". De ahí que las expectativas del leonés con 'su' nueva piloto sean máximas. Tan es así, que la burgalesa ya tiene los galones de líder del Santana Racing Team: "En la marca están todos muy felices y Cristina está contenta. Ella va a tener menos presión y eso va a hacer que progrese mucho más. Cristina es ahora la líder del equipo, todo gira en torno a ella. Y todos sabemos que no ha sido así en el pasado. Todo el mundo va a trabajar para ella y esto la va a llevar muy lejos. Habrá muchas noticias y muy buenas con Cristina", aventura. Calleja, que atiende a MARCA desde Costa Rica, donde graba un nuevo episodio de 'Planeta Calleja' junto a otra grande del deporte español como Carolina Marín, no estará en el próximo Dakar 2027 (salvo sorpresa de última hora) pero asegura que hubiese cedido su asiento a Gutiérrez si hubiese sido necesario: "Yo estoy feliz, absolutamente feliz con que Cristina esté a los mandos de Santana. Tan es así que antes de decidir si este año iba a correr el Dakar por motivos laborales, me daba igual. Habría cambiado correr yo porque corra Cristina. Lo dije desde el minuto uno: si no hay la economía para dos coches, que sea Cristina". Eso sí, el Dakar sigue formando parte de los planes de futuro del aventurero, que siempre ha reconocido que la carrera árabe es una de las experiencias más emocionantes de las muchas que ha vivido: "Yo ya volveré si procede y el futuro lo dice. Yo no soy un piloto profesional como ella, tengo otro trabajo y en función de ello hay años que puedo correr y otros que no. Pero Cristina es una solvencia absoluta". Santana está en buenas manos.

articles.title: La Fórmula 1 ya ruge en Madrid: “Ha sido un reto muy difícil y casi un gran milagro”
articles.standfirst: Mariano de Paco, consejero de Cultura, Turismo y Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid, destacó en 'La Tribu' el impacto económico y deportivo, con más de 120.000 visitantes
articles.summary: Mariano de Paco, consejero de Cultura, Turismo y Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid, destacó en 'La Tribu' el impacto económico y deportivo, con más de 120.000 visitantes
articles.body: Mariano de Paco pasó por La Tribu en la antesala de un fin de semana histórico para Madrid. El consejero de Cultura, Turismo y Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid analizó la llegada de la Fórmula 1 a la capital, con el circuito de Madring en las inmediaciones de IFEMA y con Fernando Alonso y Carlos Sainz como grandes reclamos nacionales. “Son días de estar despierto, contento y esperando el gran acontecimiento que sin duda nos va a convertir en esa región capital del deporte del mundo”, afirmó De Paco. Para el dirigente, la cita trasciende lo deportivo y confirma la capacidad de Madrid para atraer grandes eventos internacionales. De Paco explicó que la Fórmula 1 llega a Madrid después de años de trabajo, ilusión y convencimiento. Según señaló, el proyecto nació como un sueño y se ha ido convirtiendo en realidad hasta situar a la Comunidad como sede del Gran Premio de España durante una década “y muchísimo más”. “Madrid ahora mismo es el lugar donde todos los grandes eventos quieren estar, es el lugar donde el público quiere venir a disfrutar de ellos”, aseguró. El consejero defendió además que la apuesta encaja con un modelo de turismo ordenado y con una idea amplia del deporte: “El deporte es cultura”. Uno de los grandes argumentos del proyecto está en sus cifras. De Paco aseguró que el Gran Premio superará los 460 millones de euros de impacto sobre la economía madrileña y sobre el Producto Interior Bruto. Además, habló de más de 8.000 puestos de trabajo asociados a la prueba. El consejero proyectó ese impacto a largo plazo: “Durante diez años estamos hablando de casi 5.000 millones de impacto económico y social”. Una dimensión que, según explicó, no solo beneficia al sector deportivo, sino también al tejido profesional, económico y laboral de la región. La previsión de asistencia también es muy elevada. Mariano de Paco avanzó que más de 120.000 personas acudirán a Madrid durante el fin de semana del Gran Premio, de las cuales más de 80.000 llegarán desde fuera de la región y unas 40.000 desde fuera de España. El consejero también subrayó el escaparate global de la Fórmula 1. Recordó que la competición alcanza cifras “apabullantes” de seguimiento internacional, con más de 1.500 millones de espectadores a lo largo del año y alrededor de 100 millones por cada Gran Premio. De Paco admitió que la gran dificultad de este primer año ha sido construir el circuito. A diferencia de futuras ediciones, en las que el foco estará más centrado en la semana del evento, esta primera cita obligaba a “bajar el sueño a tierra” y levantar una instalación nueva. “Había que planificar y construir un nuevo circuito, un nuevo circuito que además es inédito, es único en el mundo”, explicó. El consejero aseguró que esa prueba “se ha pasado con creces” gracias al trabajo de IFEMA, las administraciones y todas las personas implicadas para que el Gran Premio cumpla la normativa y cause el menor perjuicio posible a la ciudad. El dirigente madrileño reconoció que el camino no ha sido sencillo. Las lluvias complicaron los plazos de asfaltado y obligaron a pausar algunos trabajos hasta que el firme estuviera seco y en condiciones óptimas. Aun así, defendió que el proyecto ha salido adelante con los estándares de calidad exigidos. “Ha sido un reto muy difícil y casi un gran milagro”, afirmó De Paco. El circuito, según explicó, ya está testado por los pilotos y preparado para recibir al público y escuchar por fin el rugido de los motores. “Esto no se va a quedar aquí, sino que ha llegado para quedarse”, defendió. Madrid afronta así su primer gran fin de semana de Fórmula 1 con una mezcla de ambición, impacto internacional y desafío logístico. La expectativa, según el consejero, es poder decir el domingo que se ha hecho “el mejor Gran Premio del mundo” y empezar desde ahí a superarlo.

articles.title: "Es un buen sitio para Alonso, porque con los muros marca la diferencia"
articles.standfirst: Honda habla de haber encontrado el "camino correcto" tras Monza en cuando a la manejabilidad del nuevo motor
articles.summary: Mike Krack confirma que la dificultad extrema y
articles.body: Optimismo en Honda y optimismo en cuanto a una buena posible actuación de Fernando Alonso en Aston Martin. Mike Krack, jefe de operaciones, confía en el talento de Fernando en las pistas difíciles, en lo que considera "un circuito extraordinario". Por su parte Shintaro Orihara dice que han conseguido optimizar el motor tras Monza y habla de haber encontrado "el camino correcto". "En los Países Bajos tuvimos algunos problemas de conducción, así que implementamos algunas medidas correctivas en Monza, principalmente en el sistema de combustión", decía el ingeniero jefe de Honda F1 en Madring. "Lo importante es lograr una combustión estable y una entrega de par constante. Observamos un buen progreso en los datos de la FP1 y recibimos comentarios positivos de los pilotos tras la sesión. Luego, optimizamos la configuración de datos durante el fin de semana de carrera y funcionó bien, como lo demuestran los comentarios positivos de los pilotos al segundo día", dice sobre lo sucedido en Monza. "Así que encontramos el camino a seguir. Después de Monza, llevamos todos los datos y comentarios al banco de pruebas y aplicamos nuevas medidas correctivas para mejorar la conducción. Siempre debemos mejorar la conducción paso a paso, pero hemos encontrado el camino correcto", asegura sobre un mejor rendimiento en conjunto en esta pista, que además no tiene una dependencia de los caballos puros como la del pasado fin de semana. Por su parte, Mike Krack, el portavoz del equipo en los circuitos como jefe de operaciones de Aston Martin, elogió lo que se ha construido en Madrid en pocos meses. "Obviamente, todo el mundo ve las tomas de a bordo, simulaciones o datos del simulador, pero cuando ves las subidas y bajadas, los desafíos, los muros, la curva rápida a la derecha con peralte... Creo que han hecho algo realmente extraordinario aquí. Veremos cómo resulta, pero creo que a primera vista hay que ser muy positivo con lo que se ha logrado en este tiempo, porque construir un circuito en medio de la ciudad, alrededor de un centro de exposiciones, puede ser muy aburrido, pero creo que este no lo será", aseguraba. Y cree que le irá bien a Alonso por muchos motivos. "Sí, creo que cuando ves este trazado y los muros tan cerca, creo que el piloto puede marcar la diferencia. No en todos los circuitos, pero hay algunos donde creo que el piloto puede marcar la diferencia, así que es bueno tenerlo con nosotros. Me gustan estos circuitos donde un piloto se debe adaptar, digamos, y sí, confío en que veremos a nuestros pilotos rendir bien", decía incluyendo a Stroll. La pista sucia del viernes también es un lugar en el que Fernando se mueve bien. "Sabemos que cuando las condiciones de agarre son muy malas y todo es nuevo, hemos visto actuaciones sobresalientes de su parte. Recuerdo en Qatar, hace dos o tres años, cuando hubo una tormenta de arena y la pista era muy, muy lenta, y él fue a veces cuatro o cinco segundos más rápido que todos. Así que podríamos ver algo similar en la FP1, pero luego están la FP2 y la FP3 para que todos se pongan al día", dice sabiendo que los rivales irán aprendiendo poco a poco.
